meta.description: Watches the owner's UNIVERSITY mailbox (Microsoft 365 / Outlook) and only wakes an agent when mail actually arrives. Ships pointed at ostimteknik.edu.tr → Ultron. The scan runs through Mark VI's own Microsoft connection — no second credential, no model, no tokens. Everything is configured in ONE node: 'Domain list'. This is the Outlook twin of 'Mail watch', which does the same job for Gmail; they are separate workflows because they are separate mailboxes, not two views of one.

nodes.name: Every 10 minutes
nodes.notes:
University mail arrives at any hour — an exam room change at 23:00 is exactly the case this exists for — so this runs around the clock. 144 scans a day, each one HTTP request and zero tokens.

Every rule in the list is checked on this one schedule. Widening it to */30 only delays a push; the SPEDA-Seen category means a longer gap can never lose a message.

nodes.name: Domain list
nodes.notes:
⚙️ EDIT HERE — the whole configuration surface. One block per domain, in the DOMAINS array. The comment block documents every field.

Each entry becomes one item and every node downstream runs once per item, so watching the university AND the student information system needs no other change.

TO FORK: duplicate the workflow, keep only the rules you want in it, rename it, activate. Rules in different workflows are independent.

nodes.name: Igor: scan Outlook
nodes.notes:
The cheap half. One Microsoft Graph request through Igor's own connection, a strict sender-domain check, and a category test — no model anywhere in it.

neverError so a Graph outage becomes a status the Gate can report ONCE, instead of a failed execution nobody reads.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.notes:
The cost boundary — everything downstream spends money, everything upstream does not. On a normal run every rule reports zero and this returns no items, which stops the branch.

pairedItem is set explicitly so the mark-seen node can find its own rule's message ids.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ ({ "payload": { "type": "watchdog", "event": "new_school_mail", "job": "outlook_watch", "automation": "School mail watch — " + $json.domain, "source": "outlook", "domain": $json.domain, "count": $json.count, "messages": $json.messages, "intent": $json.alert ? ("Your school-mail watch for " + $json.domain + " cannot read the Microsoft mailbox right now (" + $json.detail + "). Tell the owner in one short line that the watch is blind and Microsoft 365 likely needs reconnecting in Settings → Connections. Do not call any tool.") : $json.intent }, "output_mode": "push" }) }}

nodes.name: Igor: trigger agent
nodes.notes:
THE EXPENSIVE HALF — one agentic turn per rule that found mail. The agent comes from the rule (Ultron by default), so the URL is an expression; nothing to edit here.

No neverError, deliberately: a failure must kill the branch BEFORE mark-seen, leaving the mail uncategorised so the next poll retries it. Retries cover the 503 the trigger endpoint returns when the turn registry is at capacity.

nodes.name: Igor: mark seen
nodes.notes:
Categorises exactly the messages just handed to the agent, so the next scan skips them. This is what stops the same mail pushing every 10 minutes. Unread state is untouched — the mail still looks new in Outlook.

$('Gate').item — not .first() — so when two rules both find mail, each ack categorises ITS OWN messages.

Deliberately AFTER the trigger: categorising first would lose a message whenever the notify call failed. On the blind-watch alert path message_ids is empty and this is a no-op.
